steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The criminal justice system involves: police (investigate), CPS (prosecute), courts (try), sentencing (punish), probation (supervise in community), prison (custodial sentences). | Key Fact: The police are responsible for preventing and detecting crime, maintaining public order, and protecting life and property. Police officers have powers of arrest, stop and search, and detention. | Key Fact: The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) reviews evidence gathered by the police and decides whether to charge — applying the Full Code Test (sufficient evidence + public interest). | Key Fact: Trial by jury is available for serious criminal offences ('indictable offences') in the Crown Court. The jury of 12 citizens decides the verdict; the judge decides the sentence.
